packet.source_section:
## Failure handling — alerting an operator

Many dead-letter events for one tenant in a short time usually mean something systemic. The threshold is tuned so that a brief burst does not page an operator while a sustained fault does.

Normative rule
1. When five dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within any rolling thirty-minute window, Orion must raise an operator escalation.
2. The window is rolling: at each new dead-letter event Orion must count the events for that tenant in the preceding thirty minutes, including the new event.

Example
Tenant T-7 produces dead-letter events at 08:20, 08:25, 08:31, 08:40 and 08:49. At 08:49 five events fall within the preceding thirty minutes, so an escalation is raised.

question: After T14 (IE2 and the authority step), do the live claims at the address designated for locus J state every required proposition — [J-3] an operator escalation is raised when five dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within any rolling thirty-minute window; [J-4] the window is rolling: at each new dead-letter event the events for that tenant in the preceding thirty minutes, including the new one, are counted — with no two live claims stating the same meaning, and no live claim stating a meaning that contradicts them, belongs to another locus, or was never in the source? None of these may still be current: [J-1] an operator escalation is raised when three dead-letter events occur for the same tenant within one hour; [J-2] the one-hour window is measured from the first of the three events. Optional descriptive statements may be present if faithful: J-o1, J-o2.
